Title: February 5, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting
Overview: The February 5, 2026 regular council meeting covered public concerns over the South Boulder Recreation Center, a Black History Month declaration, a rezoning of 5501 and 5505 Arapahoe Avenue to MU-4, the 2026 policy statement on regional, state, and federal issues, House Bill 26-1010 (the HOME Act), and council priorities and process improvements. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda and both rezoning ordinances, and it directed staff to pursue several amendments to House Bill 26-1010 after a straw poll. Staff said recreation center decisions would return to council in March and May, while the policy statement additions and retreat priorities were discussed without a formal vote recorded.

Topic1.Title: South Boulder Recreation Center Future and Open Comment
Topic1.Summary: Numerous residents spoke during open comment urging the city to keep the core amenities of the South Boulder Recreation Center, including the lap pool, gym, and weight rooms, citing swim teams, seniors, youth, and accessibility. Speakers also raised concerns about funding priorities relative to office buildings and the East Boulder project. Staff responded that the city has not decided to close a facility, that a $2 million investment was approved in 2025, and that the long-term financial strategy and recreation discussions will return to council in March and May.

Topic2.Title: Black History Month Declaration
Topic2.Summary: Council member Adams presented a declaration recognizing February 2026 as Black History Month, highlighting Boulder's Black community history including early entrepreneurs, the Boulder Blues baseball team, and Second Baptist Church. Representatives from the Black Women's Alliance at CU Boulder and the Black Student Alliance spoke in response.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic3.Summary: Council approved consent agenda items 4A through 4C unanimously, with no discussion raised on the items.

Topic4.Title: Callup Check-ins for Landmark Certificates
Topic4.Summary: Staff presented two landmark alteration certificates in the Mapleton Hill Historic District, one to demolish and rebuild an accessory building at 2408 street and one to construct a new primary building at 2439 Broadway. No council members called either item up, so both proceeded without further review.

Topic5.Title: Rezoning of 5501 and 5505 Arapahoe Avenue to MU-4
Topic5.Summary: Council held a second reading and public hearing on ordinances rezoning approximately 2.65 acres at 5501 and 5505 Arapahoe Avenue from BC-1 to MU-4, plus adjacent right-of-way. Staff noted the change aligns with the East Boulder subcommunity plan and mixed-use transit-oriented designation, and the associated form-based code review was previously approved. One speaker opposed increased density, and both ordinances were adopted unanimously.

Topic6.Title: 2026 Policy Statement on Regional, State, and Federal Issues
Topic6.Summary: Staff presented recommended additions to the 2026 policy statement from the intergovernmental affairs committee, including human rights language, support for federally funded research jobs, food supply and local grower support, orphaned well cleanup, workforce housing, construction defects reform, coal ash mitigation, wildfire guidance, protections against surveillance, and data center water and energy conservation. Council members affirmed existing electrification positions and raised questions about how excessive resource use would be determined.

Topic7.Title: House Bill 26-1010 (HOME Act) Discussion
Topic7.Summary: Staff summarized state House Bill 26-1010, which would allow residential development on qualifying nonprofit, school, church, university, and transit-owned parcels of five acres or less through administrative approval in any zone. Staff outlined permitted local standards, prohibited restrictions on height and unit counts, and political context, noting the bill is a governor's priority. Council members raised concerns about loss of home rule, lack of affordability requirements, nonprofit definitions, and compatibility with the comprehensive plan. After a straw poll, council chose to pursue amendments, including tying projects to demonstrated needs, excluding unincorporated county land, tightening nonprofit eligibility, applying height standards consistent with the zone, limiting project size, and requiring comprehensive plan compatibility.

Topic8.Title: Council Retreat Follow-up on Priorities and Process Improvements
Topic8.Summary: Staff presented scoping for council priorities including bicycle security and theft reduction, wildfire home hardening and assessment, a tip credit ordinance exploration, power resiliency with Xcel Energy, and sister city program updates. Process improvements discussed included board packet timing, CAC request tracking, historic designation presentations, and limiting late meetings. Council members asked that the Title 9 rewrite be recorded as a conditional priority and requested clarity on ebike regulations, climate and agriculture work, and public safety updates.
